items.note: Also written 'goeie môre'.

items.exampleAf: Ek is jammer, ek is laat.

items.exampleEn: Excuse me, where is the bank?

items.note: Very common: food, weather, a good time.
Informal 'you'; formal is 'u'.
Also means 'his' (sy boek = his book).
Also 'that/which' in the middle of a sentence.
Also means 'true' (dis waar = it's true).
'Waarom' means the same.

items.af: Aangesien sy die buurvrou nie ken nie, stel sy haarself voor.
items.en: Since she doesn't know the neighbour, she introduces herself.
wrongEn: Since she knows the neighbour well, she introduces herself.
Although she doesn't know the neighbour, she introduces herself.
Since the neighbour doesn't know her, she introduces herself.
Since she didn't know the neighbour, she ignored her.
wrongAf: Aangesien sy die buurvrou nie ken nie, sy stel haarself voor.
Aangesien sy ken die buurvrou nie, stel sy haarself voor.
Aangesien sy die buurvrou nie ken, stel sy haarself voor.
Hoewel sy die buurvrou nie ken nie, stel sy haarself voor.
items.note: After 'aangesien' (since) the verb goes last (nie ken nie); the main clause then starts with its verb: stel sy.

items.af: Nadat hulle mekaar gegroet het, het die ou vriende ure lank gesels.
items.en: After they had greeted each other, the old friends chatted for hours.
wrongEn: Before they greeted each other, the old friends chatted for hours.
After they had greeted each other, the old friends argued for hours.
After greeting each other, the old friends chatted for an hour.
After they had greeted each other, the new friends chatted for hours.
wrongAf: Nadat hulle mekaar het gegroet, het die ou vriende ure lank gesels.
Nadat hulle mekaar gegroet het, die ou vriende het ure lank gesels.
Voordat hulle mekaar gegroet het, het die ou vriende ure lank gesels.
Nadat hulle mekaar gegroet het, het die ou vriende ure lank gegesels.
items.note: 'Nadat' (after) sends 'gegroet het' to the end. 'Gesels' already starts with ge-, so no extra ge-.

items.af: Die man vir wie ek gister gewaai het, is die nuwe skoolhoof.
items.en: The man I waved to yesterday is the new principal.
wrongEn: The man who waved to me yesterday is the new principal.
The man I waved to yesterday was the old principal.
The man I waved to today is the new principal.
The man I didn't wave to yesterday is the new principal.
wrongAf: Die man vir wie ek gister het gewaai, is die nuwe skoolhoof.
Die man wat gister vir my gewaai het, is die nuwe skoolhoof.
Die man vir wie ek gister waai het, is die nuwe skoolhoof.
Die man vir wat ek gister gewaai het, is die nuwe skoolhoof.
items.note: After a preposition, use 'wie' for a person: vir wie (to whom). The relative clause ends with its verb.

items.af: Die gaste is deur die gasvrou self by die deur verwelkom.
items.en: The guests were welcomed at the door by the hostess herself.
wrongEn: The guests welcomed the hostess at the door.
The guests are being welcomed at the door by the hostess herself.
The guests were welcomed at the door by the hostess's husband.
The guests were turned away at the door by the hostess herself.
wrongAf: Die gaste word deur die gasvrou self by die deur verwelkom.
Die gaste is deur die gasvrou self by die deur geverwelkom.
Die gaste het die gasvrou self by die deur verwelkom.
Die gaste het deur die gasvrou self by die deur verwelkom.
items.note: Past passive: is + past participle (is verwelkom = were welcomed). 'Word' would make it present. Ver- verbs take no ge-.

items.af: Die toeris het gevra of iemand hom die pad kon wys.
items.en: The tourist asked whether someone could show him the way.
wrongEn: The tourist asked whether he could show someone the way.
The tourist said that someone had shown him the way.
The tourist asked someone to drive him there.
The tourist asks whether someone can show him the way.
wrongAf: Die toeris het gevra of kon iemand hom die pad wys.
Die toeris het gesê dat iemand hom die pad gewys het.
Die toeris het gevra of hy iemand die pad kon wys.
Die toeris vra of iemand hom die pad kan wys.
items.note: A reported yes/no question uses 'of' (whether) and sends the verbs to the end: of iemand ... kon wys.

items.af: Ma het gesê dat die bure ons hond teruggebring het.
items.en: Mom said that the neighbours had brought back our dog.
wrongEn: Mom said that we had brought back the neighbours' dog.
Mom asked whether the neighbours had brought back our dog.
Mom said that the neighbours would bring back our dog.
Mom said that the neighbours had taken our dog away.
wrongAf: Ma het gesê dat die bure het ons hond teruggebring.
Ma het gesê dat die bure ons hond geterugbring het.
Ma het gesê dat ons die bure se hond teruggebring het.
Ma het gevra of die bure ons hond teruggebring het.
items.note: Reported speech with 'dat': the verbs go last. Separable terugbring puts ge- inside: teruggebring.

items.af: Niemand het die vreemdeling gegroet nie, hoewel hy vriendelik was.
items.en: Nobody greeted the stranger, although he was friendly.
wrongEn: Everybody greeted the stranger, because he was friendly.
Nobody greeted the stranger, because he was unfriendly.
The stranger greeted nobody, although they were friendly.
Somebody greeted the stranger, although he was unfriendly.
wrongAf: Niemand het die vreemdeling gegroet, hoewel hy vriendelik was.
Niemand het nie die vreemdeling gegroet nie, hoewel hy vriendelik was.
Niemand het die vreemdeling gegroet nie, hoewel hy was vriendelik.
Die vreemdeling het niemand gegroet nie, hoewel hy vriendelik was.
items.note: 'Niemand' (nobody) still needs a closing 'nie', but no extra 'nie' after the verb. 'Hoewel' sends 'was' last.

items.af: Hy het nooit dankie gesê nie, selfs nie nadat ons gehelp het nie.
items.en: He never said thank you, not even after we had helped.
wrongEn: He always said thank you, even after we had helped.
We never said thank you, not even after he had helped.
He never said thank you, not even before we helped.
He seldom said thank you, even after we had helped.
wrongAf: Hy het nooit dankie gesê, selfs nie nadat ons gehelp het nie.
Hy het nooit dankie gesê nie, selfs nie nadat ons het gehelp nie.
Ons het nooit dankie gesê nie, selfs nie nadat hy gehelp het nie.
Hy het altyd dankie gesê, selfs nadat ons gehelp het.
items.note: 'Nooit ... nie' (never) closes with 'nie'; 'selfs nie ... nie' (not even) closes its own clause too.

items.af: Gister het ek my ou onderwyser raakgeloop en hom dadelik herken.
items.en: Yesterday I bumped into my old teacher and recognised him at once.
wrongEn: Yesterday my old teacher bumped into me and recognised me at once.
Yesterday I bumped into my old teacher but didn't recognise him.
Yesterday I phoned my old teacher and thanked him at once.
Today I bump into my old teacher and recognise him at once.
wrongAf: Gister ek het my ou onderwyser raakgeloop en hom dadelik herken.
Gister het ek my ou onderwyser geraakloop en hom dadelik geherken.
Gister het ek my ou onderwyser raakloop en hom dadelik herken.
Gister het my ou onderwyser my raakgeloop en my dadelik herken.
items.note: raakloop becomes raakgeloop (ge- in the middle); herken keeps its form because her- verbs take no ge-.

items.af: Toe hy haar ontmoet, het hy met die deur in die huis geval.
items.en: When he met her, he came straight to the point.
wrongEn: When he met her, he fell through the door into the house.
When he met her, he beat about the bush.
When she met him, she came straight to the point.
When he met her, he left without saying a word.
wrongAf: Toe hy haar ontmoet, hy het met die deur in die huis geval.
Toe hy haar ontmoet, het hy met die huis in die deur geval.
Toe hy haar ontmoet, het hy om die warm pap gedraai.
Toe hy haar ontmoet, het hy met die deur in die huis val.
items.note: 'Met die deur in die huis val' = to come straight to the point (literally: fall into the house with the door).

items.af: Haar woorde was soos 'n koel briesie, en almal het ontspan.
items.en: Her words were like a cool breeze, and everyone relaxed.
wrongEn: Her words were like a cold wind, and everyone tensed up.
A cool breeze blew while she spoke, and everyone relaxed.
Her words were like a cool breeze, but nobody relaxed.
Her words were like a hot wind, and everyone relaxed.
wrongAf: Haar woorde was soos 'n koel briesie, en almal het geontspan.
Haar woorde was soos 'n koel briesie, en almal ontspan het.
Haar woorde was soos 'n koue wind, en almal het verstyf.
Haar woorde was soos 'n koel briesie, maar niemand het ontspan nie.
items.note: A simile (vergelyking) compares with 'soos' (like). Ontspan starts with ont-, so its past form has no ge-.

items.af: Ondanks die stortreën het die wag elke kind by die hek gegroet.
items.en: Despite the downpour, the guard greeted every child at the gate.
wrongEn: Because of the downpour, the guard greeted every child at the gate.
Despite the downpour, every child greeted the guard at the gate.
Despite the downpour, the guard didn't greet a single child.
Despite the downpour, the guard greets every child at the gate.
wrongAf: Ondanks die stortreën die wag het elke kind by die hek gegroet.
Ondanks die stortreën het die wag elke kind by die hek groet.
Weens die stortreën het die wag elke kind by die hek gegroet.
Ondanks die stortreën het elke kind die wag by die hek gegroet.
items.note: When a phrase like 'ondanks die stortreën' comes first, the verb stays second: het die wag.

items.af: As ek geweet het dat die gaste so vroeg sou opdaag, sou ek hulle ingewag het.
items.en: Had I known the guests would arrive so early, I would have waited for them.
wrongEn: Because I knew the guests would arrive so early, I waited for them.
Had I known the guests would arrive so late, I would have waited for them.
Had I known the guests would arrive so early, I would not have waited.
Had the guests known I would arrive so early, they would have waited for me.
wrongAf: As ek geweet het dat die gaste so vroeg sou opdaag, ek sou hulle ingewag het.
As ek geweet het dat die gaste so vroeg sou opdaag, sou ek hulle inwag het.
As ek geweet het dat die gaste sou so vroeg opdaag, sou ek hulle ingewag het.
Omdat ek geweet het dat die gaste so vroeg sou opdaag, het ek hulle ingewag.
items.note: Unreal past: as ... het, sou ... het (if I had ..., I would have ...). Separable inwag becomes ingewag.

items.af: Die ministers is plegtig ontvang, waarna hulle deur die burgemeester voorgestel is.
items.en: The ministers were formally received, after which the mayor introduced them.
wrongEn: The ministers formally received the mayor, after which they introduced him.
The ministers were formally received, after which they introduced the mayor.
The ministers are being received, after which the mayor will introduce them.
The ministers were received without ceremony, before the mayor introduced them.
wrongAf: Die ministers het plegtig ontvang, waarna hulle deur die burgemeester voorgestel het.
Die ministers is plegtig geontvang, waarna hulle deur die burgemeester voorgestel is.
Die ministers is plegtig ontvang, waarna hulle is deur die burgemeester voorgestel.
Die ministers word plegtig ontvang, waarna hulle deur die burgemeester voorgestel word.
items.note: Two past passives (is ontvang, voorgestel is). 'Waarna' (after which) sends 'is' to the end. Ont- verbs take no ge-.

items.af: Die voorsitter het meegedeel dat nuwe lede voortaan deur 'n komitee verwelkom sou word.
items.en: The chair announced that new members would henceforth be welcomed by a committee.
wrongEn: The chair asked whether new members could henceforth be welcomed by a committee.
The chair announced that a committee would no longer welcome new members.
The chair announced that new members had always been welcomed by a committee.
A committee announced that new members would henceforth be welcomed by the chair.
wrongAf: Die voorsitter het meegedeel dat nuwe lede sou voortaan deur 'n komitee verwelkom word.
Die voorsitter het gemeedeel dat nuwe lede voortaan deur 'n komitee verwelkom sou word.
Die voorsitter het gevra of nuwe lede voortaan deur 'n komitee verwelkom kon word.
'n Komitee het meegedeel dat nuwe lede voortaan deur die voorsitter verwelkom sou word.
items.note: Formal reported speech with a future passive in the past: verwelkom sou word (would be welcomed). Meedeel: meegedeel.

items.af: Die hoflikheid waarmee hy vreemdelinge bejeën, is iets waaruit ons kan leer.
items.en: The courtesy with which he treats strangers is something we can learn from.
wrongEn: The courtesy with which strangers treat him is something we can learn from.
The rudeness with which he treats strangers is something we can learn from.
The courtesy with which he treated strangers is something we never learnt.
He treats strangers courteously because he learnt it from us.
wrongAf: Die hoflikheid waarmee hy bejeën vreemdelinge, is iets waaruit ons kan leer.
Die hoflikheid waarmee hy vreemdelinge bejeën, is iets waaruit ons leer kan.
Die hoflikheid waarvan hy vreemdelinge bejeën, is iets waaruit ons kan leer.
Die hoflikheid waarmee vreemdelinge hom bejeën, is iets waaruit ons kan leer.
items.note: Two relative clauses with waar- words: waarmee (with which), waaruit (from which). Verbs go last in both.

items.af: Toe die vreemdeling haar aanspreek, het sy met die mond vol tande gestaan.
items.en: When the stranger addressed her, she was lost for words.
wrongEn: When the stranger addressed her, she stood with a mouth full of teeth.
When the stranger addressed her, she answered at once.
When she addressed the stranger, he was lost for words.
When the stranger addressed her, she laughed at him.
wrongAf: Toe die vreemdeling haar aanspreek, sy het met die mond vol tande gestaan.
Toe die vreemdeling haar aanspreek, het sy met die mond vol tande staan.
Toe die vreemdeling haar aanspreek, het sy dadelik geantwoord.
Toe sy die vreemdeling aanspreek, het hy met die mond vol tande gestaan.
items.note: 'Met die mond vol tande staan' = to be lost for words (literally: stand with a mouth full of teeth).

items.af: Haar glimlag was 'n masker waaragter sy haar teleurstelling probeer verberg het.
items.en: Her smile was a mask behind which she tried to hide her disappointment.
wrongEn: She wore a smiling mask to hide her disappointment.
Her smile was a mask behind which she tried to hide her delight.
Her smile showed openly how disappointed she was.
Her smile was a mask behind which she hid her anger.
wrongAf: Haar glimlag was 'n masker waaragter sy haar teleurstelling geprobeer verberg het.
Haar glimlag was 'n masker waaragter sy probeer haar teleurstelling verberg het.
Sy het 'n masker met 'n glimlag gedra om haar teleurstelling te verberg.
Haar glimlag was 'n masker waaragter sy haar vreugde probeer verberg het.
items.note: A metaphor (metafoor) says the smile IS a mask, with no 'soos'. Probeer + another verb takes no ge-: probeer verberg het.

items.af: Geen hoflikheid kon die spanning verlig nie, en niemand wou die eerste stap doen nie.
items.en: No courtesy could ease the tension, and nobody wanted to take the first step.
wrongEn: Courtesy eased the tension, and everybody wanted to take the first step.
No courtesy could ease the tension, but somebody took the first step.
They showed no courtesy, so nobody wanted to take the first step.
No courtesy will ever ease the tension, because nobody takes the first step.
wrongAf: Geen hoflikheid kon die spanning verlig, en niemand wou die eerste stap doen nie.
Geen hoflikheid kon die spanning verlig nie, en niemand wou nie die eerste stap doen nie.
Geen hoflikheid kon die spanning verlig nie, en niemand wou die eerste stap gedoen nie.
Hoflikheid kon die spanning verlig, en almal wou die eerste stap doen.
items.note: Each negative clause (geen ..., niemand ...) closes with its own 'nie'. 'Die eerste stap doen' = take the first step.

items.af: Omdat etiket hoog geag word, het die skool 'n werkswinkel vir matrieks gereël.
items.en: Because etiquette is highly valued, the school arranged a workshop for matrics.
wrongEn: Although etiquette is highly valued, the school cancelled the matric workshop.
Because etiquette is seldom valued, the school arranged a workshop for matrics.
Because the matrics arranged a workshop, etiquette is now highly valued.
Because etiquette is highly valued, the school will arrange a matric workshop.
wrongAf: Omdat etiket hoog word geag, het die skool 'n werkswinkel vir matrieks gereël.
Omdat etiket hoog geag word, die skool het 'n werkswinkel vir matrieks gereël.
Omdat etiket hoog geag word, het die skool 'n werkswinkel vir matrieks gegereël.
Hoewel etiket hoog geag word, het die skool die werkswinkel vir matrieks afgestel.
items.note: A passive inside an 'omdat' clause ends 'geag word'; the main clause then inverts: het die skool.
